prompt: On-call is woken at 3am for high CPU, though users noticed nothing.
why: Alert on what users feel, not every cause.
trap: CPU is useful on a dashboard, not as a page.

prompt: With 200 alerts a day, the team started ignoring them, including the real one.
why: Too many alerts cause fatigue. Alert on symptoms.
trap: It's not a missing signal; it's too many pages.

prompt: The page fires when more than 2% of checkout requests fail for five minutes.
tells: more than 2% of checkout requests fail
why: User-facing error rate is a symptom worth paging on.
trap: It's not a probe removing an instance; it's paging a person.

prompt: Alerts fire when the error budget is being spent fast enough to run out in two days.
tells: fast enough to run out in two days
why: Burn-rate alerts tie paging to user impact.
trap: It's SLO-based, but the question is when to page.

prompt: Disk at 80% opens a ticket for the morning instead of paging.
tells: opens a ticket for the morning
why: Not every cause needs a page. Save pages for symptoms.
trap: It's not scaling; it's routing the alert.

prompt: Users couldn't log in for an hour, but no alert fired because every server looked healthy.
why: Watching causes missed the symptom. Alert on user outcomes.
trap: Health checks passed; the alert was on the wrong thing.
